PC: Intern reviews sign-out and recognizes that the patient is admitted for pneumonia.
Intern interviews Patient and learns that this shortness of breath came on suddenly and she has never had it before.
Intern conducts brief physical exam and auscultates an irregular rhythm as well as rales in the right lung base.
Intern re-assesses patient as heart rate rises to 150 beats er minute, and the monitor alarms.
Intern orders an EKG and chest xray, STAT BMP
Intern begins an IV beta blocker (Metoprolol 5mg IV) or calcium channel blocker (Diltiazem 15mg IV).
Intern determines next management steps as patient stabilizes.
Intern provides medications that may produce harm (eg Albuterol) or doses that are deleterious (“Metoprolol 50mg IV now”).
MK: Intern recognizes atrial fibrillation on the EKG and right lower lobe infiltrate on the chest x-ray.
Intern may mis-interpret the shortness of breath as COPD exacerbation.
Intern mis-reads the chest x-ray as “Normal”, “CHF”, “PE”.
Intern fails to properly assess patient as stable and attempts cardioversion, intubation etc.
SBP: Intern calls senior resident for help.
ICS: Give appropriate orders to the Nurse
Intern interviews the Nurse and is provided with current vitals and re-assuring documentation from prior notes in the chart.
